answer: Shard custody stops bulk fake identities: each identity must hold real data. A nebula of shards is split by beacon draw, one unique shard per identity, so no two share the same bytes. Each identity locks a 40-credit bond and passes a key-signed retrieval challenge each epoch. Auditors wander the assignment map; a rented shard fails its key-bound challenge and burns its bond. The kth fake needs a kth shard and bond, so 1,000 fakes lock 40,000 credits, while one honest agent locks 40. An identity that cannot serve its shard stands as an island with no reward.
